teaching: A greeting opens a conversation. Hello works at many times. Good morning is for the morning; good evening is for meeting someone in the evening. Good night usually ends an evening conversation. In I am fine, I is a subject pronoun, am is a linking verb, and fine describes the subject. A question with be puts the verb before the subject: Are you ready? Thank you and goodbye help close an exchange.
foundationEvidenceLimit: These mixed items sample the allocated strands. They are not five unseen items per child objective and do not establish EF-AC02/03 mastery.

conceptChecks.prompt: In Hello, I am Ana, which word is a greeting?
In I am fine, which word names the speaker without using a name?
conceptChecks.answer: I; it is a subject pronoun.

conceptChecks.prompt: In I am fine, what is the complete predicate?
conceptChecks.answer: am fine; fine is a subject complement, not an object.

conceptChecks.prompt: Why is Are you ready? a question rather than You are ready? in the neutral written pattern?
conceptChecks.answer: Are comes before the subject you; the sentence ends with a question mark.

conceptChecks.prompt: Which usually closes an evening visit: Good evening or Good night?
conceptChecks.answer: Good night; Good evening normally greets someone.

pronunciationSelfReview: Replay the greeting clip. Notice the stress in MORning and THANK you. Record your own greeting if you wish; compare whether the greeting and reply can be understood. Text alone cannot show pronunciation.
workplaceApplication: Greet a receptionist and ask for repetition: Could you say that again, please?
quietPolicy: Use the existing quietText alternative for guidedSpeaking. Text records communication/grammar attempts only; speaking and pronunciation remain unassessed.

support.beforeAttempt: Offer teaching, original examples and replay on request; record use as support.
support.afterAttempt: Reveal the example only after the first attempt; preserve the original and label retries.
support.repairPhrase: Could you say that again, please?
support.privacy: Invented names, families, homes, work and prices are valid; no retained private recording is required.

coreCompletionProposal.rule: Attempt every required core activity with the existing speaking/quiet substitution, review examples/corrections, and attempt self-review. Accuracy never gates participation completion.
coreCompletionProposal.additionalConceptChecks: Editorial sidecar only; not silently added to core completion.
coreCompletionProposal.baselineAndDelayed: Optional, separate journals; not core or vocabulary schedule credit.

assessment.communication: Record which requested message components are conveyed, absent, or not assessed; accept effective alternatives.
assessment.grammar: Record target opportunities and first-response forms individually; do not infer opportunities from prompt presence.
assessment.vocabulary: Use existing itemId plus senseId. Exposure and productive use do not schedule recognition.

reading.acceptedAlternatives: Short factual answers and equivalent paraphrases matching the passage; no exact-string scoring.

listening.acceptedAlternatives: Short factual answers or equivalent paraphrases matching the recording; reading a transcript is assisted text evidence.

assessment.speaking: Only an actual recorded/listened-to attempt supports speaking evidence; human listener records intelligibility with qualifications/conditions.
assessment.pronunciation: Unassessed without qualified listening to retained/consented audio; no acoustic inference from text or ASR.
assessment.thresholds: No new numeric pass or CEFR threshold selected. Existing EF/IL criteria require their recorded review.
assessment.comparison: Baseline before teaching; ordinary practice separate; unfamiliar context plus fresh day-7/day-28 prompts. Log support, modality, actual interval and prior exposure. These tasks are not calibrated comparable forms.
